Chapter 11: Living from the Ground of Stillness
As your journey deepens, you start to realize something surprising—stillness isn’t just a fleeting pause or some special state you have to work for.
It’s actually the ground of your being.
Think of it as a silent presence that’s always underneath every thought, every feeling, every single experience. Most people only notice this stillness in rare, quiet moments...but honestly, it’s always right here, just waiting to be recognized.
Picture this: you wake up before dawn, while the world is still dark and hushed. There’s this gentle sense of possibility in the air, a kind of freshness.
Your mind hasn’t started racing with plans or worries yet. In that space, can you feel it? There’s a sense of being held by something vast—and deeply gentle. The day hasn’t begun, but peace is already present.
Most folks don’t realize that this same stillness is available anytime—even right in the middle of a hectic day.
It’s not about escaping from life or chasing after special experiences.
It’s about recognizing that silent presence underneath it all, no matter what’s happening on the surface.
I remember a friend telling me about their busy workdays. In the middle of all the chaos, they’d pause for just a few seconds, close their eyes, and notice the stillness inside.
Even with phones ringing and emails flying, that quiet presence was always there—a kind of inner refuge, a real source of strength. Over time, those small moments of stillness became the foundation for everything else in their life.
Living from this stillness doesn’t mean you avoid challenges or tough emotions.
It’s more about meeting each moment from a place of openness and trust. Your mind will still think, your heart will still feel—but now, there’s a deeper sense of being rooted in something unchanging.
And here’s the beautiful part: this way of living is open to everyone, no matter what’s going on in your life.
All it takes is the willingness to pause, to listen, to notice the quiet that’s always present.
When you start living from stillness, life becomes less about striving, and more about simply being.
You meet each moment with more presence, more compassion, and a little more joy.
